answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to post a stake bond that vests slowly, like a pearl forming layer by layer, so a fresh identity starts with near-zero trust and must earn standing through verified work over time. Timber offers the right analogy: one cheap fake is easy, but forging a whole forest of long-lived, bonded identities costs far more than any single scam can return. The bond is also a signal to peers: honest agents gladly stake because they expect to keep it, while an attacker loses real value per fake identity, making mass fakery uneconomic.
